instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Recognize AH as IPsec integrity and data-origin authentication without confidentiality; retain contextual cryptographic/protocol support with precise numbered scope withheld.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: HOLD authentication as unique-person identity or safe plaintext. AH excludes mutable IP-header fields and does not encrypt; anti-replay effectiveness requires receiver checks and sound security-association/key handling. Header changes such as NAT complicate deployment. AH is not ESP, tunnel/transport mode, an authenticated-encryption construction or proof of IPsec configuration competence. Preserve prior AH-card context-only scope; no packet, replay window, peer or VPN was configured or tested.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Recognize DKIM as verification of covered canonicalized message content under a signing domain, not automatic visible-author authentication or a safety verdict.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: HOLD message origin as visible From alignment, human authorship or trusted content. Verification binds signing domain d= to covered selected headers and canonicalized body, potentially limited by l=; it does not promise all-byte immutability, encryption or safe attachments. Key retrieval/trust, algorithms and custody matter. DMARC alignment is a separate check. Preserve the existing DKIM support identity lacking 4.5 as a metadata mismatch, not an approved schema edit; no DNS lookup or signature was verified.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Recognize DMARC as Author Domain alignment using a passing SPF or DKIM result, with requested handling/reporting policy rather than mandatory universal receiver action.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: HOLD coordinates SPF and DKIM as requiring both to pass: one passing aligned identifier is sufficient. SPF envelope/HELO, DKIM signing domain and visible Author Domain are distinct identities with strict/relaxed alignment rules. Requested reject/quarantine/report handling remains subject to receiver policy; pass is not encryption, guaranteed delivery, trustworthy content or human identity. Use current RFC9989 rather than superseded RFC7489; no DNS policy, mail flow, receiver decision or report was tested.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Recognize DNSSEC as origin authentication and integrity for signed DNS data through validated trust, not encrypted DNS transport; precise numbered implementation scope withheld.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: HOLD validate responses as universal protection from poisoning or all DNS threats. Validation needs appropriate trust anchors, chain, signatures and time/algorithm handling; unsigned/insecure, bogus and indeterminate states must remain distinct. Signed origin does not imply safe destinations or availability. DNSSEC supplies no query confidentiality and is not DoH/DoT, CAA issuance authorization or filtering policy. Existing support identity has empty codes; do not invent a precise 1.4/2.4/4.5 assessment or edit it. No resolver or DNS answer was validated.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Recognize IPsec suite context only; hold the all-encrypted and combined-AH-and-ESP reading pending explicit configuration and optional-service qualifications.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: HOLD authenticated and encrypted using AH and ESP as automatic suite-wide encryption or mandatory simultaneous protocols. AH has no confidentiality; ESP services depend on selected transforms and configuration, including integrity-only use. Security-association policy, peer/key establishment, modes and enabled receiver checks determine protection; not all traffic is automatically protected. Preserve prior AH and the inspected lesson optional-encryption premises. No precise support link or full 1.4/3.2 implementation assessment is approved; no VPN was configured.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Recognize MITM/on-path as adversary positioning to intercept or alter endpoint communications; narrow attack vocabulary, not a demonstrated cryptographic break.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: HOLD intercepts or alters as ability to read/forge any correctly authenticated encrypted channel. Attack viability depends on path/relay position, endpoint identity verification, key/protocol and user/device assumptions. Passive observation, replay, endpoint compromise and forward secrecy are separate concerns. Correct peer authentication and integrity constrain impersonation/modification; encryption alone without identity binding is insufficient. No attack, decrypted capture or prevention was demonstrated. Metadata-only MITM references are not rendered tooltip exposure.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Recognize NGFW as a network firewall capability category combining application-aware inspection and prevention features under actual product and deployment conditions.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: HOLD feature bundle as uniform enabled product, guaranteed detection/prevention, WAF/CASB/SIEM/HSM equivalence or automatic TLS payload visibility. Actual rules, inspection parsers, signatures, licenses, capacity, placement and TLS decryption/endpoint visibility govern coverage; evasion and false positives/negatives remain. Encrypted traffic may expose metadata while hiding content. TLS inspection requires an appropriate authorized termination/decryption path and trusted endpoint configuration, not simply an NGFW label. No appliance or traffic was inspected.

instructionalProposals.teachingUnderstanding: Recognize NIPS as network intrusion-prevention capability in an inline enforcement path that can block detected activity, not a guarantee that every attack is prevented.
instructionalProposals.contentQualification: HOLD can block as all malicious traffic blocked or label proving active enforcement. Inline placement, enabled prevention/rules, visibility, tuning, performance and failure behavior matter; passive observation alone does not block packets in the path. False positives can block benign traffic and false negatives can miss attacks; encrypted payloads need an appropriate observation/decryption point. NIPS is not HIPS, NIDS, generic IPS, HSM or the combined HIPS/NIPS card identity. No sensor, rule or throughput was tested.
